title: Power Circuit Test Sheet
source: spec/Power_Circuit_Test.html — the power-circuit sibling of `lighting-circuit-test.json`: the same project/location band, one circuit-by-circuit test table, the same fixed five-function instrument table, a remarks box and a three-row sign-off. It differs from the lighting sheet in what is measured — earth loop impedance and RCD trip timing at 0° and 180° are added, and the lighting sheet's Room Name and Remarks columns are absent — and in naming the two witnesses (CBRE, CxA) rather than heading both rows alike. As on the lighting sheet the supplied file was saved with the instrument make/model/serial/cert filled in (Megger MIT310, Fluke 115, Megger RCDT310, Megger LTW315, Martindale CP501); those are record values — the kit changes as instruments are recalibrated or replaced — so only the function names are carried here. The source's own "Rev : 0 / Date" footer is not reproduced as a field: the printed footer already carries the template code and revision (SPEC §7), and a second revision on the same page invites the two to disagree.

sections.title: Circuit Test Results
sections._note:
`page_break_before` on the opening section is the grouping idiom: `paginate` gives every section its own page unless at least one declares a break, and a break on the first section is a no-op for layout — it is already page 1. Same as `lighting-circuit-test.json`.

**The paper's two-level header is flattened twice over.** It spans "Insulation Resistance" across an L-N and an L-E sub-column, and "RCD Timing (ms)" across 0° and 180°; `dynamic_table` columns are flat, so each group name moves into its columns' own labels. Nothing is lost but the two spanning cells.

**Insulation readings are `text`, not `number`.** A circuit that reads above the meter's range is written ">999", which a numeric column rejects — and on an insulation test that is the normal, passing result, so it is the one reading the sheet must never refuse. Volts, earth loop impedance and the two RCD times are `number`: each is always a figure, and a numeric column is what a later `limit` (e.g. the 300 ms / 40 ms RCD bounds) would be judged against.

**Unit conflict in the source, resolved to MΩ.** The insulation column heads read "L-NΩ" and "L-EΩ" but the cells prompt "MΩ". Insulation resistance is measured in megohms and a reading in ohms would be four orders out, so the megohm prompt is taken as the correct one — the same conflict, and the same resolution, as the lighting sheet. Worth confirming against the paper master before Rev A hardens.

**No Remarks column.** The lighting sheet carries one per circuit; this one does not, and the section-level Remarks box below is the only free text on the page. Matching the original wins (SPEC §5).

The source seeds seventeen blank rows; `min_rows` is five and the engineer adds what the board needs, so a record with six circuits prints six rows rather than six plus eleven empty ones.

columns.label: Polarity
columns._note: The paper prompts a tick or a cross. Worded Pass / Fail here so the printed cell says what it means on a signed document, and so the outcome makes a failed polarity derivable as an outstanding item (SPEC §6).

sections.title: Test Instrument / Tools Required
sections._note:
**Why this section starts page 2.** Measured on the live build: a page gives 877px to content, a table row costs 35px. The circuit table alone runs to the full page once a board has any number of ways — the source's seventeen circuits fills it — so the closing blocks go overleaf and page 1 belongs to the test results. Same reasoning as `lighting-circuit-test.json`.

The five function names are the paper's fixed list and are seeded as template data; make, model, serial and certificate are the engineer's, and are not.

**Columns are the paper's four, which means no calibration DUE date.** This sheet records a certificate number, not an expiry. `link_to_instrument_register` is set for consistency with the other templates, but note it is a declarative flag today — nothing in the app reads it yet (record↔instrument linking is still to be built, see `lib/calibration.ts`). When it is built it will need a due date to judge expiry against, and this section would need a fifth column the paper does not have.

sections.title: Remarks
sections._note: A `field_group`, as on `lighting-circuit-test.json`: a `standard` section always prints its serial and remarks columns, so a lone textarea row comes out as an empty serial column plus two columns both headed Remarks. The source is a plain box; this prints as one.

sections.title: Sign-off
sections._note:
An in-flow `sign_off` section rather than the top-level `footer`: PrintView always gives the footer a page of its own, which would add a third sheet carrying nothing but signatures. Both routes carry the same slots through `collectSignatureSlots`, so the status workflow is unchanged. Same idiom as `lighting-circuit-test.json`.

The source's three rows, and unlike the lighting sheet it names the two witnesses — "Witnessed By CBRE" and "Witnessed By CxA" — so the roles read the same here; the distinct `stage` values drive the workflow (SPEC §6), with the commissioning agent taking the `client` stage as the last signature on the page.

The paper's sign block carries only Name, Signature and Date — no company. The renderer always prints Company, so Tested By defaults to Kenyon Pte Ltd and stays editable (unlocked, as on `staircase-pressurization.json`); the witness companies are seeded from the roles the paper names and stay editable too.
